log.title: The API is live on AWS
log.body: Created the stack, set three repository variables and ran the deploy workflow: it builds the image, pushes it to ECR, and the server pulls it, runs migrations, then starts the new API behind Caddy with HTTPS. The first run failed at the OIDC step. Repositories created after July 2026 send a subject that carries the owner and repository IDs (repo:OWNER@ID/NAME@ID:ref:...), so the name-only subject in the role's trust policy never matched. CloudTrail showed the real value; the template now takes the exact subject as a parameter, and the second run went green. Next: point the web app at this API.

log.title: Ready to deploy: priced first
log.body: Priced the ADR-002 demo profile before creating anything: ECS Fargate, a load balancer and RDS come to about $65-70 a month in Singapore, twice the $30 budget. The demo uses the fallback the ADR already named: one EC2 instance with Docker Compose (Postgres, API, Caddy for HTTPS), about $13 a month. One CloudFormation file creates it; GitHub Actions deploys through an OIDC role and SSM Run Command, with no SSH port and no AWS keys in GitHub. Migrations run before the new API starts.

log.title: The web app on the real API
log.body: Sign-up, onboarding and the board now run against the NestJS API: Next forwards /api/v1 to it, so the browser sees one origin and the SameSite=Strict refresh cookie just works. An expired access token is refreshed once and the request replayed; refreshes are single-flight, because the refresh token is single-use and two parallel refreshes look like theft. Screens whose endpoints come later say Coming soon. The public prototype stays on the mock API.

log.title: Drag and drop on the real API
log.body: POST /tasks/{id}/move: the client names the neighbours, the server picks a fractional key between them, so a move writes one row and never renumbers the column. The key logic is a pure function with its own unit tests; neighbours from another column, another project or in the wrong order are a 422, and a stale version is the same 409 as an edit.

log.title: Edit conflicts: 409
log.body: PATCH /tasks/{id} only writes if the task is still at the version the client read, in one statement; otherwise it answers 409 with the current task so the client can show what changed and retry. A deterministic test makes two writes race on the same version: exactly one wins. Removing the version condition fails five tests.

log.title: Tasks: create and list
log.body: Tasks on the real API: a new task goes to the bottom of its column with a fractional key, assignees must work in the same workspace, and the board list pages with a keyset cursor (status, position, id). Positions are compared byte by byte (COLLATE "C"); a test fails if a migration ever loses that. Viewers can read a board they were invited to but not write to it.

log.title: Roles and tenant isolation
log.body: Workspaces and projects on the real API. One pure function decides who may do what (owner, admin, member, viewer); outsiders get the same 404 as for something that doesn't exist, so IDs reveal nothing. 18 unit cases cover the permission table and 9 end-to-end tests try to read and write across workspaces.

log.title: First real backend: auth
log.body: NestJS API on Postgres, test first: register, login, refresh-token rotation with reuse detection, logout and /me, validated against the OpenAPI contract. A deliberately broken build showed one race test was passing by luck; it now forces the race deterministically. CI runs the API tests against a Postgres service.

log.title: System design: sequences and decisions
log.body: Sequence diagrams for the three hard flows (a move seen live across API instances via the outbox, AI drafting with rate limit and timeout, refresh-token rotation with a long-lived socket), the realtime message contract, and two ADRs: NestJS + Prisma, and AWS with demo and production profiles.

log.title: System design: containers and data model
log.body: C4 context and container diagrams and the ERD for all of v1: modular monolith (API + worker), WebSocket fan-out over Redis pub/sub, a transactional outbox for reliable events, and a schema built around tenant isolation and optimistic locking. In docs/architecture.

log.title: Ready to present
log.body: Richer demo data across three client projects, a 100-second captioned demo video on the landing page, and an 8-slide pitch deck. Next: feedback from a mentor and team leads, then the UI is frozen.

log.title: AI task drafting and activity log
log.body: Paste a client brief and get editable task drafts to review before anything is saved (rule-based stand-in for the model on the mock). Every create, edit and move now lands in a per-project activity log. Both endpoints added to the OpenAPI contract as drafts for the Stage 3 review.

log.title: Kanban board with live updates
log.body: Drag and drop with optimistic moves (mouse, touch and keyboard, announced to screen readers). Live updates arrive over a WebSocket; on the mock, virtual teammates move and add tasks, with presence avatars and toasts.

log.title: Visual v2 and landing page
log.body: New landing page (problem, features, how it works, planned pricing) with a one-click demo. Redesigned sidebar with project colours, a richer Today screen and a new sign-in page.

log.title: v1 scope locked
log.body: v1: accounts, workspaces and roles, per-project client viewers, live board with drag and drop, Today, activity log, AI task drafting. Comments, labels, attachments and search move to the v1.1 roadmap.

log.title: New process: stages with gates
log.body: After mentor feedback, work now moves in stages — problem, prototype, system design, code — each closed by a gate. Wrote the business brief and shipped this page.

log.title: Today, Project and Members screens
log.body: Overview of late and due-soon work, project task list with detail panel and edit-conflict handling, member invites with per-project client viewers. 13 Playwright checks.

log.title: Typed data layer and auth screens
log.body: openapi-fetch + TanStack Query typed from the contract; access token in memory, refresh token in an httpOnly cookie; sign-up and onboarding flow.

log.title: Mock API and first deploy
log.body: MSW handlers typed from the OpenAPI contract: roles, 409 on concurrent edits, fractional-index ordering. Deployed to Vercel.

log.title: Monorepo and API contract
log.body: pnpm + Turborepo + Next.js 16. OpenAPI 3.1 contract with generated TypeScript types and a CI check that they stay in sync.
